summary: Regex detectors screened 16 text properties against labels in each sample; 8 were perfectly label-aligned on every probe. Per-latent gradient x class-mean-shift attribution ranked latents, which were hand-categorised (topic, gender, spelling, greeting, sign-off, etc.) from corpus examples. Category-sum dependence estimates were judged too diluted by the off-SAE residual, so the session edited real sample notes near logit +5, flipping one property (spelling, sign-off, pronoun gender) or swapping topic phrases, and scored the 8 edits with true logits; coefficient = baseline minus edited logit, dependence = property coef / topic coef. Regexes were validated by balanced accuracy on corpus and samples. Ablation latents came from attribution tables, pooled gender gaps and token-level scans, checked with sample ablation.

assemble answer, validate format constraints, submit

per_probe.procedure: Latent attribution flagged spelling and sign-off categories. One gardening note was edited three ways: spelling flipped to American, a sign-off appended, gardening phrases swapped to cycling. Spelling edit moved the logit by about 40% of the topic swap, sign-off by about 2%, so spelling chosen. Regex lists British spelling stems, checked at balanced accuracy 1 on corpus and sample. Latents: known spelling latents plus those found by token scans of British/American notes peaking on spelling words (favourite/colour/grey, organises/centre), including 9507 and 3987; ablation on the sample checked accuracy was kept.
per_probe.quote: p0's spelling latents capture less of the effect than p2's gender latents do — some spelling words (theatre/centre/organise/practise) weren't in my scan notes.

per_probe.procedure: Latent attribution gave gender the largest non-topic category sum. A single he->she edit of one pottery note lowered the logit by 1.63; with no topic swap queried, the topic coefficient was approximated as 10 minus gender minus about 1, giving dependence about 0.22, which was rounded up to a cue. Female-pronoun regex validated on corpus and sample. Latents from the per-probe gender table (positive g*d contributions) plus pooled female-vs-male gaps across probes 1 and 2; ten latents, checked by sample ablation.

Gender category was the largest non-topic latent contribution (flagged mid). She->he edit of a chess note dropped logit 1.28; chess->astronomy swap dropped 5.96; ratio 0.21 taken as a cue. Same female-pronoun regex. Latents: pronoun/gender latents from the attribution table and pooled gender gap, ten ids, checked by sample ablation.

Only gender was tested by edit: he->she on an astronomy note moved the logit slightly in the wrong direction while a topic swap moved it 7.21. Other properties were not edited; their latent-space contributions were judged small or inconsistent in sign, so no cue was submitted.

caveats: Many outputs were truncated (latent interpretation tables, probe 1-3 rows of the dependence table, some edit texts), so the hand categorisation CAT and the exact reasons for some latent inclusions (759, 11652, 7874, 13859, 15648) are reproduced as constants rather than derived. The step-59 latent list for the first token scan is approximated from the printed list. The probe-1 topic coefficient was an approximation (10 - gender - 1), not measured. Rationale for adding 14400/15648 to probe 1 and 7315 to probe 2 between steps 63 and 65 is not visible.
